tools.name: runtime_inspect_file
tools.description: Identify a program file or application bundle from its content (a Linux, Windows, macOS or Android program, a script, an installer package) and say which runtime could run it on this computer. The file is read, never executed. Only files the assistant has been given access to for this task can be inspected.

path.description: The full path of the file or bundle.

tools.name: runtime_autopilot_plan
tools.description: Say what the compatibility autopilot would try for a Windows application that fails under Wine, in which order and why, and which remedies it would not try and why. Nothing is run or changed. The autopilot itself only ever works in throwaway copies of the application's prefix; applying a remedy it found is the person's decision, made outside the assistant.

app_id.description: The identifier of an installed Windows application, such as org.example.app. Without it the plan is made from the failure class alone.

failure.description: The failure class to plan for. Without it, the class of the application's latest autopilot result, or every class.

tools.name: runtime_autopilot_results
tools.description: List the compatibility autopilot's results for a Windows application: what failed, what was tried, what made it work, how long it took, and which remedies are applied to it now. Reads only.

app_id.description: The identifier of an installed Windows application, such as org.example.app.

tools.name: runtime_mac_identify
tools.description: Say what a macOS application, disk image, installer package or program is, and whether Darling, TUR's experimental macOS layer, can be expected to start it: which processors it is built for (an Apple-silicon-only application is refused with the reason), whether it uses Swift or SwiftUI (which Darling does not run), whether it is encrypted. The file is read, never run or unpacked. A disk image's or package's contents are analysed only when it is installed. It never says an application works; only a recorded run says that.

path.description: The full path of the .app bundle, .dmg, .pkg, zip archive or program.

tools.name: runtime_mac_list
tools.description: List the macOS applications installed in Darling on this computer: name, version, bundle, the Darling build and mode each was installed with, and what the analysis found when it was installed. Reads only.

tools.name: runtime_mac_status
tools.description: Say whether TUR's build of Darling is on this computer: not published for this processor, published and not fetched yet (it is fetched when the first macOS application is installed), ready, or damaged; which Darling commit it is. Reads only; fetches nothing.

tools.name: runtime_mac_install
tools.description: Install a macOS application the person has (a .app bundle, .dmg, .pkg or zip archive) into a Darling prefix of its own, inside the sandbox, fetching TUR's Darling build first when it is not here. Consequential: it downloads Darling (hundreds of megabytes) and uses disk space; it is the person's decision.

package.description: The full path of the package.

tools.name: runtime_mac_uninstall
tools.description: Remove an installed macOS application: its Darling prefix, its private home with whatever it saved there, its record, launcher entry and logs. Consequential and not reversible; it is the person's decision.

app_id.description: The identifier of an installed macOS application, such as org.example.app.
